title: Operation Detectives
goal: I can solve multi-step problems with the four operations. I can use bar models for "times as many" and work backwards through a number machine.

learn.intro: A bar model shows a "times as many" story. Each equal part is one unit. To go back to the start of a number machine, undo each step in the opposite order.

example.problem: Mr Tan has 3 times as many red pens as blue pens. He has 156 pens in all. How many blue pens does he have?
steps: Blue is 1 unit and red is 3 units. That is 4 units.

example2.problem: I think of a number. I add 9 and then multiply by 4. The answer is 68. What is my number?
steps: Undo the steps in the opposite order.

howto.title: How to solve it
steps: Bar models: draw one bar for each quantity. Count the units.
Divide the total by the number of units.
Machines: start from the end and undo each step. Check by going forward.

try.text: A shop has 114 pens and rulers. The number of pens is 5 times the number of rulers. How many rulers are there? {b}
try.explanation: Rulers are 1 unit and pens are 5 units: 6 units in all. 6 units = 114, so 1 unit = 114 ÷ 6 = 19 rulers.

items.text: Find the value of each.
Round each number to the nearest 1000. Then estimate the answer.
A hall has 28 rows of 36 chairs. Then 45 chairs are broken and taken away. How many chairs are left in the hall? {b} chairs
items.explanation: 28 × 36 = 1008 chairs at first. 1008 − 45 = 963 chairs are left.

items.text: A baker packs 5468 buns into boxes of 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many full boxes does she fill? {b} boxes

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many buns are left over? {b} buns

items.explanation: 5468 ÷ 8 = 683 with a remainder of 4, because 8 × 683 = 5464 and 5468 − 5464 = 4.

items.text: A farm has 4 times as many hens as ducks. There are 385 hens and ducks in all. How many ducks are there? {b} ducks
items.explanation: Ducks are 1 unit and hens are 4 units: 5 units in all. 5 units = 385, so 1 unit = 385 ÷ 5 = 77 ducks.

items.text: A ruler and a pencil case cost $47 together. The pencil case costs $9 more than the ruler.
items.explanation: Take away the extra $9: $47 − $9 = $38. Two equal parts are $38, so the ruler costs $38 ÷ 2 = $19. The pencil case costs $19 + $9 = $28.

items.text: Mei picks a secret number. She multiplies it by 6, takes away 9, then divides by 3. She gets 31. What is her number? {b}
A number trick. Start with a number. Multiply by 3, add 12, then divide by 3. Last, subtract the number you started with.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Whatever you start with, you end with {b}

items.explanation: 6 × 3 = 18, 18 + 12 = 30, 30 ÷ 3 = 10, 10 − 6 = 4. 15 gives 45, 57, 19, 4. × 3 then ÷ 3 gives back the number, the 12 ÷ 3 adds 4, and taking away the number leaves 4.

items.text: Find the missing numbers.
Mrs Lee buys 6 notebooks at $3 each and 4 pens at $2 each. She pays with $50. What is her change? ${b}
In a chain, add the last 2 numbers to make the next number. Fill in the missing numbers.
Kumar picked 3 times as many mangoes as Aisha. They picked 480 mangoes in all. How many more mangoes did Kumar pick than Aisha? {b} mangoes
items.explanation: Aisha has 1 unit and Kumar has 3 units: 4 units in all. 1 unit = 480 ÷ 4 = 120. Kumar has 360 and Aisha has 120. The difference is 2 units: 240.

items.text: Rule: do brackets first, then × and ÷, then + and −. Work from the left.
items.hint: In part (a), do 4 × 9 and 12 ÷ 3 before anything else.

items.text: A number tower has 3 numbers at the bottom: 5, a missing number and 11. Each number above is the sum of the 2 numbers just below it. The top number is 52. What is the missing number? {b}
items.hint: Write the 2 numbers in the middle row. They add up to 52.
items.explanation: The middle row is 5 + ? and ? + 11, and these add up to 52. So 5 + 11 + 2 × ? = 52, 2 × ? = 36 and ? = 18. The middle row is 23 and 29.

items.text: Kumar and Siti have 90 stickers altogether. Kumar has 5 times as many as Siti. Kumar gives some stickers to Siti. Then they have equal amounts.
items.hint: Each of them ends with half of the 90 stickers.
items.explanation: Siti is 1 unit and Kumar is 5 units. 6 units = 90, so 1 unit = 15. Siti has 15 and Kumar has 75. Equal shares are 45 each, so Kumar gives 75 − 45 = 30.

items.text: Rule: brackets first, then × and ÷, then + and −.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Put ONE pair of brackets in 7 + 3 × 8 − 4 to make 76. Write the numbers inside the brackets: {b} + {b}

items.hint: For (a), estimate first. A big answer needs ×.
items.explanation: (a) 9 × 4 = 36 and 36 − 6 = 30. The other signs do not give 30. (b) (7 + 3) × 8 − 4 = 10 × 8 − 4 = 76. Brackets round 3 × 8 give 7 + 24 − 4 = 27, and brackets round 8 − 4 give 7 + 3 × 4 = 19.

items.text: Ben and Mei both save for a bike. Plan A: start with $15 and save $8 each week. Plan B: start with $0 and save $13 each week.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In which week do both plans have the same amount? Week {b}

items.hint: Fill in the table. Look at the gap between the plans each week.
items.explanation: Plan A has $15, $23, $31, $39. Plan B has $0, $13, $26, $39. Both have $39 in week 3. Each week Plan B gains $5 on Plan A, and the start gap is $15, so 15 ÷ 5 = 3 weeks.

items.text:
Fill in the missing digits.
3 □ 4 × 7 = 2 □ 3 8
items.hint: Start with the ones: what is 4 × 7?
items.explanation: 4 × 7 = 28, which ends in 8, as needed. 3□4 × 7 = 2128 + 70 × □ must be 2□38. Trying 3 gives 2128 + 210 = 2338. Check: 334 × 7 = 2338. So both missing digits are 3.

There are 4 times as many red cars as blue cars. There are 275 cars in all. How many red cars are there? {b}
items.explanation: Blue is 1 unit and red is 4 units: 5 units. 1 unit = 275 ÷ 5 = 55. Red is 4 × 55 = 220.
